title: Binary search tree
statement: Start simple: Build a binary search tree with insert, contains, and inorder. inorder returns values separated by spaces. Inserting a duplicate does nothing. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: An empty tree has an empty inorder string.
think: Each node has a value, left child, and right child.
The search comparison chooses the side.
A duplicate matches the current node and stops.
Inorder visits left, node, then right, which yields sorted values.
hints: Use recursion or an explicit parent walk.
Create the child only when the link is null.
Build the inorder string while traversing.

tests.name: sorted
tests.call: { Bst t = new Bst(); t.insert(2); t.insert(1); t.insert(3); return t.inorder(); }

tests.name: contains
tests.call: { Bst t = new Bst(); t.insert(2); return t.contains(2) + ":" + t.contains(4); }

tests.name: duplicate
tests.call: { Bst t = new Bst(); t.insert(2); t.insert(2); return t.inorder(); }

tests.name: left-chain
tests.call: { Bst t = new Bst(); t.insert(3); t.insert(2); t.insert(1); return t.inorder(); }

tests.name: mixed
tests.call: { Bst t = new Bst(); t.insert(5); t.insert(1); t.insert(8); t.insert(3); return t.inorder(); }
